title: Bofanglutide (GZR18): The Once-Monthly GLP-1 That Could Redefine Long-Term Obesity Management — Research Dossier
excerpt: Bofanglutide (GZR18) is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist from Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals designed for once-monthly subcutaneous injection. Phase 3 GRADUAL-3 met its primary endpoint on November 4, 2026, confirming that weight loss achieved on biweekly dosing is fully maintained on monthly administration — a potential paradigm shift for obesity pharmacotherapy.
content:
What Is Bofanglutide?

Bofanglutide (research code: GZR18) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist developed by Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals, a Chinese biopharmaceutical company. Its most distinctive feature is an extended pharmacokinetic profile that enables subcutaneous administration as infrequently as once every four weeks (once monthly) — compared to the weekly injections required for semaglutide and tirzepatide.

On November 4, 2026, Gan & Lee announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 GRADUAL-3 maintenance trial, confirming that weight loss achieved during 52 weeks of biweekly dosing is successfully maintained when patients transition to once-monthly bofanglutide. The company describes this as the first completed global Phase IIIb sequential study to evaluate monthly-dosing maintenance via a randomized controlled design.

Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

Mechanism of Action

Bofanglutide binds and activates the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) — the same target engaged by semaglutide and liraglutide. GLP-1R activation in the brain reduces appetite and food intake; in the pancreas it potentiates glucose-dependent insulin secretion; and in the gut it slows gastric emptying. What distinguishes bofanglutide is its molecular engineering for prolonged half-life, enabling the Q4W (every-four-weeks) maintenance dosing schedule that sets it apart from the crowded weekly GLP-1 field.

Key Research Findings

GRADUAL-1 — Phase 3 (China, 52 Weeks)

  • Population: ~630 Chinese adults with obesity or overweight without adequate response to diet/exercise
  • Dosing: biweekly subcutaneous injection (24 mg vs 48 mg vs placebo)
  • Results:
    • 24 mg arm: −15.12% mean body weight vs −1.11% placebo
    • 48 mg arm: −18.54% mean body weight vs −1.11% placebo
  • Safety: consistent with GLP-1 RA class (predominantly mild-to-moderate GI AEs during dose escalation)

GRADUAL-3 — Phase 3 Maintenance (Results: November 4, 2026)

  • Design: 24-week randomized maintenance phase; patients previously treated with biweekly bofanglutide for 52 weeks transitioned to once-monthly (Q4W) dosing
  • Primary endpoint: change in body weight at week 24 of maintenance phase
  • Result: Primary endpoint met — once-monthly bofanglutide maintained weight loss achieved during the induction phase
  • Safety: favorable profile across all dose groups; no new safety signals identified; GI adverse events mild-to-moderate and transient
  • Significance: First global Phase IIIb study demonstrating randomized evidence for monthly-maintenance GLP-1 dosing strategy

GRADUAL-2 — Phase 3 vs. Wegovy (Ongoing)

  • 52-week active-comparator trial pitting bofanglutide against semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly in adults with and without type 2 diabetes
  • Results pending; this trial will be pivotal for establishing bofanglutide's competitive positioning

US Phase 2 Study (Results: June 2026)

  • Bofanglutide met its primary endpoints in a Western-population Phase 2 study, announced June 2026
  • Specific efficacy numbers pending publication; establishes the US regulatory pathway

Dosing in Research

All dosing information reflects investigational research protocols only.

  • Induction phase: subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks, dose-escalating to 24 mg or 48 mg
  • Maintenance phase: subcutaneous injection once every 4 weeks (once monthly) — the GRADUAL-3 paradigm
  • Standard precautions for GLP-1 RA class apply (GI tolerability, pancreatitis risk, thyroid C-cell monitoring)

FAQ

What makes bofanglutide different from weekly GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic?

The key distinction is dosing frequency. Bofanglutide's long-acting design enables monthly subcutaneous injection, compared to weekly injections for semaglutide and tirzepatide. The GRADUAL-3 Phase 3 trial (positive November 4, 2026) confirmed that transitioning patients from biweekly to once-monthly dosing successfully maintained weight loss. Monthly dosing could substantially improve adherence and reduce injection burden. Bofanglutide is a GLP-1 mono-agonist; it does not add GIP receptor agonism as tirzepatide does.

How much weight loss did bofanglutide produce in clinical trials?

GRADUAL-1 Phase 3 (52 weeks, biweekly, Chinese adults): 15.12% mean weight reduction at 24 mg and 18.54% at 48 mg versus 1.11% for placebo. GRADUAL-3 confirmed maintenance of that weight loss on monthly dosing. A US Phase 2 study also met its primary endpoints (June 2026).

Is bofanglutide approved in the US or Europe?

No. Bofanglutide is fully investigational as of November 2026. The US Phase 2 met its endpoints, clearing the path toward an IND and Phase 3 program in Western populations. It is not available outside authorized clinical trials. Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved. Consult a healthcare provider.

Research Limitations

  • GRADUAL-1 and GRADUAL-3 were conducted in Chinese populations; generalizability to other ethnic groups pending GRADUAL-2 and Western Phase 3 data
  • GRADUAL-3 topline data only — full efficacy numbers and peer-reviewed publication pending
  • No published head-to-head data versus semaglutide yet (GRADUAL-2 ongoing)
  • Long-term cardiovascular outcomes data not yet available
  • Mechanism is GLP-1 mono-agonism; whether monthly dosing maintains comparable efficacy to weekly tirzepatide's dual agonism remains to be demonstrated

Disclaimer

Bofanglutide (GZR18) is an investigational compound in clinical trials. This article is for educational and research purposes only. It is not medical advice and does not constitute a recommendation for use. Bofanglutide is not approved by the FDA, EMA, or any other major regulatory agency for the treatment of obesity or any condition.
